title: Bypassing Layer Boundaries (Closed Layer Violations)
pattern: A high-level layer (like UI or Presentation) bypasses the immediate business logic layer to directly query or modify low-level infrastructure/database resources.
why_bad: It breaks the architectural closed-layer contract, resulting in extremely tight coupling. Any change to the database schema or data mapping rules will instantly break the UI layer, preventing independent modifications.
detection: Static analysis checks that flag imports of database/persistence packages inside user interface or presentation modules.
counterexample: Simple, read-only CQRS read-models designed explicitly to bypass complex domain logic for high-performance rendering. Marked `Context-dependent`.
fix: Force the UI component to request data through a dedicated Service or Query layer facade.
source: *Fundamentals of Software Architecture* by Mark Richards and Neal Ford (2020), p. 140, 163.
